// <auto-generated/>
#nullable enable

namespace Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection {
    using global::Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.Extensions;
    using global::ValidationModules;
    using global::ValidationModules.Naming;

    /// <summary>Registers every validator this assembly generated.</summary>
    public static class GeneratorTestsValidationExtensions {

        /// <summary>
        /// Adds this assembly's generated validators, and a validation runner for each
        /// validated type.
        /// </summary>
        /// <remarks>
        /// <b>Not idempotent.</b> Calling this twice registers every validator twice, and a
        /// runner merges every registered validator for a type - so each error would be
        /// reported twice. Add rather than TryAdd is deliberate: registering a second
        /// validator for one type is how a hand-written rule composes with the generated
        /// one, so this cannot dedupe without breaking that.
        /// </remarks>
        public static IServiceCollection AddGeneratorTestsValidators(this IServiceCollection services) {
            services.AddSingleton<IValidatorFor<global::Sample.Pet>, global::Sample.PetValidator>();
            services.AddSingleton<IValidatorFor<global::Sample.Toy>, global::Sample.ToyValidator>();

            services.AddValidationRunner<global::Sample.Pet>();
            services.AddValidationRunner<global::Sample.Toy>();

            // TryAdd, so a namer the consumer registered first survives. The policy here is
            // the one the literals above were emitted with, so the engines that resolve a
            // namer at run time agree with the generated code by default.
            services.TryAddSingleton<IValidationFieldNamer>(CamelCaseFieldNamer.Instance);

            return services;
        }
    }
}

using System.Text.RegularExpressions;
using ValidationModules;

namespace Sample;

public sealed partial class PetValidator : IValidatorFor<global::Sample.Pet> {

    private IValidatorFor<global::Sample.Toy>[]? _toysValidators;

    /// <summary>Resolved from the container: the full set for each nested type.</summary>
    public PetValidator(
        System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable<IValidatorFor<global::Sample.Toy>> toys) {
        var resolvedToys = System.Linq.Enumerable.ToArray(toys);
        _toysValidators = resolvedToys.Length == 0 ? null : resolvedToys;
    }

    /// <summary>Standalone: nested types fall back to their own generated validators.</summary>
    public PetValidator() { }

    private IValidatorFor<global::Sample.Toy>[] ToysValidators =>
        _toysValidators ??= new IValidatorFor<global::Sample.Toy>[] { new global::Sample.ToyValidator() };

    public void Validate(ref ValidationContext ctx, global::Sample.Pet value) {
        if (value.Toys is { } entriesToys) {
            foreach (var pair in entriesToys) {
                if (pair.Value is not null) {
                    var entryCtx = ctx.PushKey("toys", pair.Key?.ToString() ?? "");
                    var entryValidators = ToysValidators;
                    for (var vi = 0; vi < entryValidators.Length; vi++) {
                        entryValidators[vi].Validate(ref entryCtx, pair.Value);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// The same tests as <see cref="Validate"/>, returning at the first failure and building
    /// no path, message or error record - a caller wanting only a boolean pays for nothing else.
    /// </summary>
    public bool IsValid(global::Sample.Pet value) {
        if (value.Toys is { } entriesToys) {
            foreach (var pair in entriesToys) {
                if (pair.Value is not null) {
                    var entryValidators = ToysValidators;
                    for (var vi = 0; vi < entryValidators.Length; vi++) {
                        if (!entryValidators[vi].IsValid(pair.Value)) return false;
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        return true;
    }
}


// ==== Sample.ToyValidator.g.cs ====
// <auto-generated/>
#nullable enable

using System.Text.RegularExpressions;
using ValidationModules;

namespace Sample;

public sealed partial class ToyValidator : IValidatorFor<global::Sample.Toy> {

    public ToyValidator() { }

    public void Validate(ref ValidationContext ctx, global::Sample.Toy value) {
        if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(value.Name)) ctx.AddRequired("name");
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// The same tests as <see cref="Validate"/>, returning at the first failure and building
    /// no path, message or error record - a caller wanting only a boolean pays for nothing else.
    /// </summary>
    public bool IsValid(global::Sample.Toy value) {
        if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(value.Name)) return false;
        return true;
    }
}
